string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China. It is a global center for politics, culture, and international communication. The city is renowned for its rich history, including iconic landmarks like the Forbidden City and the Great Wall. As a municipality, it operates directly under the central government. Beijing has successfully hosted both the Summer and Winter Olympics, making it the first city to do so. It also serves as a major hub for education, housing top universities.

Shanghai is a major global financial center and the most populous urban area in China. Located on the eastern coast, it is a direct-administered municipality. The city is famous for its modern skyline, particularly the Lujiazui financial district with the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower. Shanghai is also a cultural hub, blending traditional Chinese heritage with Western influences, evident in its historic Bund waterfront and diverse architectural styles. It boasts the world's busiest container port.

Chongqing is a major municipality in southwestern China, known for its mountainous terrain and role as a key industrial and transportation hub. It is situated at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. The city is famous for its spicy cuisine, particularly hot pot, and its dramatic night views. Because of its hilly landscape, it is often referred to as a "mountain city." Chongqing is also a significant economic center and the only municipality in western China.

Tianjin is a major coastal municipality in northern China, serving as a vital port and economic center. Located near Beijing, it is an important hub for maritime trade and industry. The city features a mix of historical architecture, including European-style buildings in the former concession areas, and modern landmarks like the Tianjin Eye ferris wheel. Tianjin is also known for its unique local culture, including traditional crosstalk comedy and its own distinct culinary traditions.
